purpose: What each source's own terms say about quoting it, read once and written down so that neither a permission nor a refusal has to be worked out twice. The site promises in six languages that an organisation may ask not to appear; this is where that promise is kept, and where a reading of a published notice is recorded with the sentence it rests on.

sources.quote: no se permite la reproducción y/o publicación, total o parcial, del sitio web, ni su tratamiento informático, su distribución, su difusión, ni su modificación, transformación o descompilación, ni demás derechos reconocidos legalmente a su titular, sin el permiso previo y por escrito del mismo
sources.finding: The notice reserves reproduction and publication of the site, in whole or in part, to prior written permission, and limits the material to personal and private use, so this project cannot quote it — and every record here rests on quoted words. Linking is a separate question and the same notice answers it the other way: it contemplates third-party hyperlinks that open the full page and say nothing misleading.
sources.route: Permission is reserved rather than refused. Asking in writing would settle it, and the operator publishes its address in the same notice.

sources.quote: La reproduction des contenus est autorisée à titre pédagogique sous réserve des conditions suivantes : [...] Citation explicite de la (ou les) source(s) du document, y compris les images. [...] Gratuité de la diffusion. [...] Tous les liens vers la page d’accueil ou l’une des pages internet du site, ainsi que tous les liens directs ou profonds vers un contenu, nonobstant leur forme, sont interdits, sauf autorisation expresse de l’éditeur du site.
sources.finding: The notice authorises reproduction for educational use on three conditions this project meets — content unaltered, source cited explicitly, distribution free — and then forbids every link to the site, home page or deep, without express authorisation. A record needs both, so no record may cite it. Recorded as two answers rather than one because a first reading saw only the permission and stopped there.
sources.route: The link ban is what stands in the way, and the notice reserves authorisation rather than refusing it. Asking the publisher would settle it.
